Short answer: Do not cancel first. Build and test the replacement while the current site stays live, then move the domain and redirects only when booking, forms, email, analytics, and ownership are ready.

What this means for your business

A website move is a chain of dependencies, not a page copy. The dangerous parts are usually domain access, forms, scheduling, old URLs, email records, and the moment traffic switches.

What to watch

  • The domain and site controlled by different unknown accounts.
  • Acuity, Square, or another booking flow treated as page content.
  • Old URLs with traffic but no redirect plan.
  • Email DNS changed while moving the website.

Do this next

  1. Inventory pages, URLs, forms, booking, domain, DNS, email, analytics, and assets.
  2. Build the new site without changing the live domain.
  3. Test every action on phone and desktop.
  4. Switch in a named window, watch errors, and keep a rollback.

When Little Fight fits

We handle the connected move and hand back the accounts, code, data, and instructions. If Squarespace still fits, staying put may be the safest answer.
